Thanks for the redline, Maya. Quick read-through notes for Lifeline’s counsel:
- Structural: Redwood can accept most commercial redlines but we prefer to keep the DPA baseline intact and handle jurisdiction-specific addenda (UK Addendum / IDTA) rather than changing core clauses. This reduces divergence across customers and speeds signature.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV is the authoritative list; we can provide a signed attestation that the listed subprocessors are engaged and have controls mapped to SOC2 categories.
- TIA scoping: I’ve attached a one-page scoping note (tia-scoping-notes.md) that outlines: data categories (tokenized customer inputs, minimal telemetry, logs), flow diagram summary, and which instruments apply (SCCs for EU transfers; UK Addendum + IDTA for UK-resident data).

Request for Lifeline: please confirm the following so we can finalize artifacts quickly:
1) Are you expecting all production inference traffic to remain within EU regions (eu-west-1) at the outset?
2) Do you require a customer-managed CMK provisioned before signing, or will you accept Redwood-managed keys with KMS attestation and a plan to enable CMK within 30 days of go-live?

If you confirm #1 and accept the CMK timeline in #2 we can finalize the TIA note and route the DPA via DocuSign by end of next week.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Legal & Privacy

Attachments: tia-scoping-notes.md (markdown)
